# Investor Outreach

Curated by Skill Harbor: an investor-communication skill for fundraising outreach that is short, concrete, and easy to act on. It covers cold emails (subject, why-this-investor opener, pitch, one concrete ask, sign-off), warm intro requests with a forwardable sub-100-word blurb that makes life easy for the connector, a default follow-up cadence (day 0, day 4 to 5 with one new data point, day 10 to 12 with a clean close, then stop), and post-meeting updates with the specific thing discussed and one new proof point. Core rules: personalize every outbound message, keep the ask low-friction, proof instead of adjectives, and never send copy that could go to any investor. The hard-bans list kills "I'd love to connect", "excited to share", generic thesis praise, and begging language; if personalization context is missing, it says the draft still needs personalization instead of pretending it is finished. It defers voice to brand-voice (also in this batch) rather than building a parallel voice system. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: personalization sources (portfolio companies, public thesis, mutual connections) must come from you, it will not invent them; it drafts, it does not send or track replies for you. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
